::: {.bnr-manual-flag .bnr-manual-flag--technical}
Technical Manual
:::

## What this step does

Mortality Step 2 reads the private all-deaths dataset from Step 1 and applies the fixed BNR Heart and Stroke death-classification rules.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Procedure at a glance"}
1. Run Step 2 for the same year and month as Step 1.
2. Confirm `Completed successfully`.
3. Check the classification, review and source-structure summaries.
4. Resolve any unexplained result before Step 3.
:::

## Before you start

- Complete Step 1 successfully for the same year and month.
- Understand that this is a practical approximation of underlying cause of death, not formal ICD-10 coding or a replacement for DORIS automated cause-of-death software.
- Do not change terminology, evidence classes or classification rules during a routine data release.

The evidence classes are Clear, Likely, Possible, Mention only and No evidence. The public definitions are:

- **Primary:** Clear + Likely;
- **Inclusive:** Clear + Likely + Possible.

You can read more about the exact [CVD death-classification rules](../../reference/cvd-death-classification-rules.qmd) here.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Input files"}

| File | What Step 2 uses or checks |
|---|---|
| `$BNR_DATA_RAW/redcap/mortality/yYYYY/mMM/bnr_mort_s1_YYYYMM.dta` | Private Step 1 analytical source. Confirm the year and month match the intended mortality data release. |

:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Code files"}

| File | How it is used |
|---|---|
| `scripts/stata/mortality/bnr_mort_s2_classify.do` | Main Step 2 controller; run directly by the menu, dialog or command. |
| `scripts/stata/mortality/bnr_mort_s2_rules.do` | Applies the classification rules automatically. |
| `scripts/stata/mortality/bnr_mort_s2_rule_dictionary.csv` | Maintained list of named classification rules. |
| `scripts/stata/mortality/bnr_mort_s2_nosology.csv` | Maintained disease-term dictionary used by the classifier. |
| `scripts/stata/mortality/bnr_mort_s2_variable_dictionary.csv` | Describes the classified variables. |
| `scripts/stata/mortality/bnr_mort_s2_methods.md` | Maintained technical description of the classifier. |
| `scripts/stata/dialogs/bnr_mort_s2_classify.dlg` | Stata dialog for the year, month and replacement choice. |
| `scripts/stata/menu/bnr_menu.do` | Adds Step 2 to the BNR Stata menu. |

:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Output files"}

Step 2 writes private files to `$BNR_DATA_DERIVED/mortality/yYYYY/mMM/`.

| File | What it contains or what to check |
|---|---|
| `bnr_mort_s2_YYYYMM.dta` | Classified private mortality data used by Step 3. It still contains internal identifiers and death-certificate text. |
| `bnr_mort_s2_YYYYMM_summary.csv` | Counts by classification. Check the pattern is plausible for the period. |
| `bnr_mort_s2_YYYYMM_review.csv` | Records selected for focused human review. A review flag does not itself change the classification. |
| `bnr_mort_s2_YYYYMM_structure_summary.csv` | Source-record structure checks. Investigate unusual certificate structure. |
| `bnr_mort_s2_YYYYMM_manifest.yml` | Generated description of the input, classifier version and Step 2 files. |
| `$BNR_PRIVATE_LOGS/bnr_mort_s2_YYYYMM.log` | Private run log. |

Direct identity and linkage fields such as name, address and national registration number are removed, but all Step 2 files remain private.

:::

## Run Step 2

1. In Stata, choose **User > BNR > Update CVD mortality dashboard > Step 2: Classify causes of death**.
2. Enter the same year and month used in Step 1, leave replacement unticked for the first run, and select **Classify**.
3. Alternatively, enter the complete routine command in the **Stata command window**:

   ```stata
   do "$BNR_STATA/mortality/bnr_mort_s2_classify.do" 2026 7
   ```

4. For a deliberate rebuild, enter the complete replacement command:

   ```stata
   do "$BNR_STATA/mortality/bnr_mort_s2_classify.do" 2026 7 replace
   ```

5. In `MORTALITY STEP 2: OPERATIONAL RUN SUMMARY`, confirm `Run status: Completed successfully`.
6. Open `bnr_mort_s2_YYYYMM_summary.csv` and check the classification totals.
7. Open `bnr_mort_s2_YYYYMM_review.csv` and investigate the highlighted certificate wording and structure.
8. Open `bnr_mort_s2_YYYYMM_structure_summary.csv` and investigate any unexpected source structure.
9. Do not continue until each unusual result is explained or corrected at source.

## Change control

A change to disease terminology, evidence classes, causal rules or scenario membership requires a new classifier-definition version and renewed validation. It is not part of a routine mortality data release.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="If Step 2 does not complete"}

| Situation | Action |
|---|---|
| A required Step 1 variable or source structure has changed | Confirm whether the REDCap structure was intentionally changed. Correct the source structure or update and validate the classifier before rerunning. |
| An unusual source value stops classification | Correct the mortality record in REDCap and rerun from Step 1. Do not edit Step 1 or Step 2 generated files. |
| Existing Step 2 files block an authorised rebuild | Use the complete `replace` command and repeat all Step 2 checks. |

Read `$BNR_PRIVATE_LOGS/bnr_mort_s2_YYYYMM.log` for the exact stopping point. For other problems, see [Troubleshoot the workflow](../../maintenance/troubleshooting.qmd).

:::
